description: Find the smallest positive integer x.
solution_sketch: List integers that are ≡ 3 (mod 7): 3, 10, 17, 24, … Check each against the mod-5 condition: 3 mod 5 = 3, 10 mod 5 = 0, 17 mod 5 = 2 ✓. So x = 17. (Equivalent CRT route: write x = 3 + 7k, need 7k ≡ −1 (mod 5), i.e. 2k ≡ 4, so k ≡ 2, k = 2, x = 17.)
difficulty_rationale: Naive route: scan integers 1, 2, 3, … testing both remainders — up to 17 tests, too much bookkeeping under 40 s. Insight: fix the harder modulus (mod 7 → 3, 10, 17, …) and only test that short list against the other congruence. After the insight there are two residue lookups (10 mod 5, 17 mod 5) before the hit. Not a 20 s puzzle because a solver must hold two constraints simultaneously and iterate a candidate sequence while checking the second — a first-look 20 s solver stalls picking which modulus to iterate from.
